title: "Week 6 – Regression on respondents"

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at Part 3](../../slides/trust-one-day.html#/part-3-reproduction-and-exploration){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

This week is the reproduction and the statistics behind it. The model that the original author (OA) fitted is a regression of distrust on concern with a long list of controls, fitted to respondents who are grouped in country-rounds and countries, and every one of those features is a decision with consequences: which controls to hold constant, whether the countries and rounds enter as fixed effects or as random intercepts, whether the respondents are weighted, and how the uncertainty is judged when a hundred thousand answers come from only sixteen countries. In class you reproduce the value that Multi100 recorded for analyst 6U3LL and find out what it depends on. The modules of the week take each decision apart, two of them on the EU-frames panel, where the same models are fitted to country-years: read them with sixteen countries of respondents in mind in place of twenty-seven countries of years.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Slides, Part 3, to the menu | In class. The instruction of Task 2 of Multi100 read word for word and the aim of the reproduction; after the task, what the number depends on, the two rebuilds of the data from the survey files and why they part ways over the vote controls; then the methods slides on comparisons within country-rounds, fixed against random intercepts, and scales against their single items. | 35 minutes |
| Task 3 in your report or working script, or [Browser lab](../../cases/trust/lab.qmd#task-3-reproduction) Task 3 | In class. `fetch_multi100()` makes sure that the file of the analysts is in place, and the chunk of Task 3 fits the model of Table 3 of the paper without the unemployment rate, with random intercepts for countries and country-rounds, using `lme4::lmer()`. It gives *t* = 46.625 on 72,733 respondents, the value that Multi100 recorded for 6U3LL. The browser lab cannot read the file from the OSF and fits the closest specification of the course instead, 0.174. | 25 minutes |
| [Specification menu](../../cases/trust/menu.qmd#adjustment), the adjustment sets, and in Level 3 [countries and rounds](../../cases/trust/menu.qmd#fe) and [standard errors](../../cases/trust/menu.qmd#errors) | The four sets of controls that the curve keeps and what each holds constant; then the fixed-effects structures and the rules of inference that the menu offers, with the reason for each one that it leaves off the curve. | 30 minutes |
| [The statistical methods behind the course](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-pooled), sections 3 and 4 | Clustered standard errors and what they correct; the two fixed-effects designs; and standard errors with few clusters, the CR2 correction and the restricted wild cluster bootstrap. | 80 minutes |
| [The statistical methods behind the course](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-re), sections 5 and 6 | Within and between: random effects, why they assume that the country departures are uncorrelated with the predictor, and the within–between model that separates the two comparisons; then multilevel models fitted to respondents, the design that the OA used. | 60 minutes |
| [Weights](../../companion/weighting.qmd#sec-trust), the section on this case | The design, post-stratification and population weights of the ESS in a regression on respondents, what each makes the estimate describe, the coefficient as an average of one slope per country, and which uses of the weights stay on the curve. | 45 minutes |
| [Multiverse](../../cases/trust/multiverse.qmd#inference), inference with 16 countries | The reference specification under five rules of inference, why the respondents of one country are not independent pieces of evidence, and the wild cluster bootstrap that checks the clustered test. | 25 minutes |

**By the end of the session** you have reproduced *t* = 46.625 yourself and can say why the same specification gives 0.174 on the course extract, and you can say for the reference specification what changes, and what does not, when its country-round fixed effects become random intercepts, when it is weighted, and when its errors are clustered by country rather than treated as independent. The exercises "The model of the paper on the course data" and "How sure is the estimate?" in the section "Going further" of your report put each of those comparisons in numbers.
